title: rhamnus saxatilis subsp. villarsii
intro: Rhamnus saxatilis subsp. villarsii, commonly known as Alpine buckthorn, is a subspecies of deciduous shrub native to the mountainous regions of Europe. Alpine buckthorn has been traditionally used for its potential health benefits, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which may help to protect against cell damage, reduce inflammation, and prevent infections. The plant's therapeutic actions include cardiotonic, anti-diarrheal, and antiseptic effects, which may help to regulate heart function, alleviate digestive issues, and promote wound healing. The bioactive constituents of Alpine buckthorn include alkaloids, glycosides, and phenolic compounds, such as rhamnetin and quercetin, which have been shown to possess antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities.
